label: first copy step (echo of orig token 0, outputting token 1) in long sequences, gated by first-token identity
explanation: Almost entirely a first-copy-step unit: 94% of activation mass is at recall_idx==1 (the step right after <DEL>, where the input is original token 0 and the output is original token 1). recall_idx==1 alone gives recall 0.90 / mass recall 0.94 but precision only 0.12. Rate climbs steeply with L: about 0 for L<=5, 2.1x lift at L=9, and L>=7 holds about 97% of mass. Within that slot, which first token it is matters a lot: u, j, v, 3, t, c, 2, o, p, n carry 2-5x lift, and u gives the top activations. The second token (out_tok) has a weaker effect too: d, m, b, h, i and 0 are favoured. These look like graded, additive contributions, so no boolean rule is sharp. Best predicate (recall_idx 1, L>=7, favoured first token): dev F1 0.60, mass recall 0.81. Weak tail: about 3% of mass at the last original step (orig_idx 8, L=9) and a little at recall_idx 2. Never fires at t<6, on the delimiter step, or later in the copy phase.
